audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 was scored for Trundle while whys[0] calls it 'a genuine coin flip on execution'; 2+ items was scored for Shen while whys[6] says 'neither lane winner is decided here'; level 2 was scored 'Skill' while whys[1] says Spirit's Refuge removes your damage the moment it lands.
audit.why: 49.23% over 260 games is the flattest matchup in the slice, so the chart has to be precise rather than sweeping. Three stages disagreed with the sentence printed directly beneath them.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill / Shen / Shen / Shen / Trundle / Shen / Skill in both layers — one clean Trundle stage at his level-6 spike, which is exactly what the text argues for.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was written as a conditional spike with no way to check the condition, and Stand United's 200s cooldown was quoted in one place but not connected to the decision anywhere else.
audit.why: Stand United is 200/180/160s. That is the longest cooldown in either kit, and whether it is up is literally the go/no-go on your only winning stage.
audit.corrected: The 200s figure carried into whys[4], mid and phases[4].why as the explicit gate on the level-6 all-in.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'AS-steal' or 'AS steal' in five fields — Chomp saps Attack Damage, not attack speed. mid also says 'his Q does magic damage that your armor stacking barely touches'; Riot's Twilight Assault text says the damage is based on the TARGET'S MAX HEALTH, which is a different and more actionable fact. Shen's energy costs are never mentioned once, in either layer.
audit.why: Max-health scaling changes what you build — health stacking feeds his Q, whereas the 'magic damage' framing points you at magic resist for no reason. And Shen is the rare top laner whose limiter is energy, not cooldowns: Twilight Assault is 140 energy at rank 1 and Shadow Dash is 150, so his bar is a second cooldown timer the matchup never told you to read.
audit.corrected: All five AS references corrected to the attack-damage sap; Twilight Assault described as max-health scaling; Shen's energy costs written into early, mid and breakdown.cooldowns as 'watch his energy bar, not just his cooldowns'.

audit.whatIsWrong: Subjugate quantified as stripping 'half his armor and MR' in mid and whys[4].
audit.why: Riot's text gives a percent steal that doubles over the following 4 seconds, with no absolute figure. Half is a guess, and it is the number the whole level-6 plan is sized against.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the stated mechanic — percent of health, armour and MR on cast, doubling over 4 seconds — and the consequence that you open with it rather than finish with it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spirit's Refuge is described as blocking 'every Chomp-enhanced auto', which is right, but nothing says what still gets through or how long the block is unavailable.
audit.why: Riot's text blocks ATTACKS near his spirit blade — Chomp itself is a cast and still lands, and the zone is on 16s at rank 1 against a 3.5s Chomp. That is the difference between 'my damage is gone' and 'my autos are gone for a few seconds and then I get four bites'.
audit.corrected: whys[1], wants.you[0] and breakdown.cooldowns now give the 16s figure and separate the cast from the autos.

edits.before: Shen gets W Spirit's Refuge online and can block every Chomp-enhanced auto during a trade, shutting down the AS-steal pattern you depend on for early extended fights.
edits.after: Spirit's Refuge (16s at rank 1) comes online and blocks the autos in your trade — Chomp still lands, but the auto pattern it resets into is what he is deleting.

edits.before: Subjugate drains Shen's armor and MR onto you mid-fight, making extended trades genuinely threatening for him — your best window to force an all-in before he respects the cooldown.
edits.after: Subjugate drains a percent of Shen's health, armor and MR onto you and doubles it over 4 seconds, so open the all-in with it — this is your one clean window before he plays the cooldown.

edits.before: Force extended Chomp trades when Shen's W Spirit's Refuge is on cooldown — that is your only reliable damage window
edits.after: Force extended Chomp trades while Spirit's Refuge (16s at rank 1) is down — that is your only reliable auto window

edits.before: Use W Spirit's Refuge to block your Chomp autos and erase the AS-steal that makes your trades worth taking
edits.after: Use Spirit's Refuge to block the autos and erase the attack-damage sap that makes your trades worth taking

edits.before: Neither kit has a hard edge at level 1 — your Q AS-steal and King's Tribute sustain roughly match Shen's Ki Barrier passive shield, so the first wave is a genuine coin flip on execution.
edits.after: Neither kit has a hard edge at level 1 — Chomp's AD sap and King's Tribute sustain roughly match Shen's Ki Barrier shield, so the first wave is a genuine coin flip on execution.

edits.before: Shen's W Spirit's Refuge comes online and blocks every Chomp-enhanced auto you throw in a trade, removing the AS-steal mechanic that makes your level-2 skirmishes worth starting.
edits.after: Spirit's Refuge lands at 2 and blocks the autos in your trade for its duration — Chomp itself still connects, but the auto reset behind it is the part that was paying you.

edits.before: Shen's early armor items and passive Ki Barrier shield keep him ahead in short trades through Levels 4-5, and he can use E Taunt proactively to dictate when and where contact happens — you are reacting, not initiating.
edits.after: Shen's early armor items and Ki Barrier keep him ahead in short trades through Levels 4-5, and Shadow Dash (18s at rank 1, 150 energy) lets him dictate when contact happens — you are reacting, not initiating.

edits.before: Subjugate gives you a genuine all-in window at 6 by draining half Shen's armor and MR the moment it lands, but his R Stand United can simply send him to another lane before you complete the second cast, making it a conditional spike at best.
edits.after: Subjugate is a real all-in window at 6 — it takes a percent of his health, armour and MR and doubles that over the next 4 seconds — but Stand United is 200s at rank 1, and if it is up he simply leaves the lane, so check it before you commit.

edits.before: At level 1 neither kit dominates cleanly — you Q Chomp his first auto and steal a sliver of AD while he shields with Ki Barrier, and it roughly cancels out. Don't over-commit to a long trade here; Shen's passive shield refreshes off his own Q and you are not yet healing fast enough off King's Tribute to absorb the Ki Barrier proc plus his empowered Q hit. Play for CS, stack the AD steal with short Q trades, and watch for his W coming online at level 2 — the moment Spirit's Refuge appears, your auto-reliant damage drops to near zero inside that zone.
edits.after: At level 1 neither kit dominates cleanly — you Chomp his first auto and sap a sliver of AD while he shields with Ki Barrier, and it roughly cancels out. Do not over-commit to a long trade; his passive refreshes off his own casts and you are not yet healing fast enough off King's Tribute to absorb the shield plus an empowered blade. Play for CS, stack the AD sap with short bites, and watch two things at level 2: Spirit's Refuge appearing, after which your autos stop landing inside that zone, and his energy bar — Twilight Assault costs 140 at rank 1 and Shadow Dash 150.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 6 are Shen's clearest control window. His W blocks every Chomp auto, his E Taunt closes the gap on his terms, and his early armor itemization makes your physical burst feel soft. The play is patience: bait his E so the 18-second cooldown is running, then immediately drop Frozen Domain and Pillar behind him to cut off his retreat. Even then the trade will be close — Shen heals off his passive and his Q does magic damage that your armor stacking barely touches. Respect the matchup and look for an all-in exactly at your level 6 Subjugate spike, which strips half his armor and MR onto you in a single cast. If his R cooldown is up when you hit 6, do not all-in — he will Stand United away, reset the lane, and your power window closes.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 6 are Shen's clearest control window. Spirit's Refuge blocks the autos in every trade, Shadow Dash (18s at rank 1) closes the gap on his terms, and his early armor makes your physical damage feel soft. The play is patience: bait the dash so those 18 seconds are running, then drop Frozen Domain and Pillar behind him. Read his energy as well as his cooldowns — the dash is 150 and the blade is 140 at rank 1. Note also that Twilight Assault scales off your maximum health, so stacking HP against him pays him back. Look for the all-in exactly at your level-6 Subjugate, which takes a percent of his health, armour and MR and doubles it over 4 seconds. If Stand United is up at that moment, do not commit — 200 seconds of it means he resets the lane and your window closes.

edits.before: - Shen Shadow Dash (Taunt): matchup-defining — His engage CC. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Shen Shadow Dash: Dashes in a line, taunting all enemies hit — his engage CC. Dodge or sidestep it.
edits.after: - Shadow Dash (E): 18/16/14/12/10s, and 150 energy. His engage taunt — dodge it, then the whole cooldown is yours. - Spirit's Refuge (W): 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s. It blocks the autos, not the Chomp cast.

edits.before: Track Shen's Shadow Dash (Taunt): His engage CC. Dodge it. When it is down — Bite + duel him.
edits.after: Shadow Dash is 18s and 150 energy; Spirit's Refuge blocks autos, not the Chomp cast. Bite after both.

edits.before: W down at your feet turns short trades your way: move speed, attack speed, and healing on your own terrain. Trade only inside the zone.
edits.after: Spirit's Refuge lands and the autos in your trade stop connecting. Frozen Domain still gives you the speed, but hold the wave and farm.

edits.before: Pillar closes the kit — use it behind Shen to deny disengage, or between you and Shadow Dash (Taunt) to break his pattern.
edits.after: Pillar of Ice closes your kit — drop it behind Shen once Shadow Dash's 18 seconds at rank 1 are already running.

edits.before: Q ranks raise the bite damage and the AD steal. Keep trading in W; if Shen stands in your domain trading evenly, he is losing.
edits.after: Chomp ranks up, but Twilight Assault scales off your max health — stacking HP into him pays him back. Trade on his energy bar.

edits.before: Subjugate online — the 1v1 is yours into almost anyone the moment Shen commits. R early in the all-in so the drained resists count for the whole fight.
edits.after: Subjugate online — the steal doubles over 4 seconds, so open with it. Check Stand United first: 200s at rank 1, and if it is up he just leaves.

edits.before: With two items you out-duel Shen whenever R is up. The only loss condition left is fighting with Subjugate down — track it like he tracks Shadow Dash (Taunt).
edits.after: Two items in you are both tank-profiled and neither wins the lane outright. Subjugate still pays on Shen in a 5v5, and his map impact decides the game.

notes: I gave Shen's energy costs as raw numbers (Twilight Assault 140 at rank 1, Shadow Dash 150, Spirit's Refuge 40) and told the player to watch the bar, but I deliberately did NOT write the conclusion 'he cannot afford both back to back' — that needs Shen's maximum energy pool, which is not in the kit file. If the user can confirm the 200 pool, that line becomes the strongest sequencing cue in the matchup and belongs in mid. Also unverified and not written: whether Spirit's Refuge blocks turret shots or only champion attacks, and whether Pillar of Ice's terrain stops Shadow Dash. The claim that Twilight Assault deals magic damage was removed rather than corrected to a damage type, since Riot's text names only the max-health scaling.
